answer: One defence is a bonded reputation thread: each agent must lock a stake that is slashed if it misbehaves, and its past work forms a single verifiable thread that cannot be copied to a new identity. A fresh identity starts at the bottom, so an attacker must pay the full bond and rebuild history for every fake, like forging a ferrous chain link by link. At the zenith of trust, only long-lived, costly identities can attest, making mass fakes uneconomic.
